run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T06:56:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by its own span data: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR went from ~0-0.015/s before 06:56 to 0.50/s in the 5 minutes ending 06:56:08 and 1.93/s in the 5 minutes ending 07:01:08, while non-error ingress span rate collapsed from ~10/s to ~1.6/s. The error spans are HTTP 504 with ~15,000,000 us duration, paired with 'router frontend egress' spans of 15,000,xxx us and http.status_code 0 - i.e. the Envoy proxy gave up on its upstream (frontend) after its 15s response timeout. frontend-proxy's access log names the timed-out routes exactly: 'GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ' 504 UT response_timeout 14999ms and 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z' 504 UT response_timeout 15000ms, while GET /, GET/POST /api/cart and GET /api/data kept returning 200 in 3-303ms. The frontend side hangs on its gRPC calls: frontend p90 duration is 15000ms for the 'GET', 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' spans and for the client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and checkout's own client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct fails with gRPC status 14 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer', producing PlaceOrder gRPC 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product' and frontend POST /api/checkout 500. 100.64.188.136 is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP (port 8080). The product-catalog pod is the deepest failing dependency observed: it is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no OOMKill, ~12-13MiB of a 30Mi limit and no CPU saturation (throttled-period ratio fell from ~0.19 to ~0.03 and CPU from ~7m to ~0.3m), yet its log stream ends at 2026-11-15T07:01:21Z and its span production falls to zero, while clients get connection resets. Chaos Mesh PodNetworkChaos events targeting the product-catalog pod (product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9) begin at 2026-11-15T06:54:07Z - about two minutes before the alert's 06:56:08 onset - and recur through 07:02:07Z; they are the only non-restart events in the otel-demo namespace in the window. The exact chaos action/duration could not be read, so the injection is reported as the best-supported hypothesis for the deepest cause, with product-catalog unreachability as the observed fact.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span metrics show the error surge: 'ingress' spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR ran at 0.0037/s (5 min ending 06:41:08), 0/s (ending 06:46:08) and 0.0148/s (ending 06:51:08), then 0.5037/s (ending 06:56:08), 1.933/s (ending 07:01:08) and 1.632/s (ending 07:06:08); non-error 'ingress' span rate fell from ~10.1/s to 1.59/s over the same intervals.

Over the whole 05:56:08-07:11:08 window, frontend-proxy accumulated 1349.77 'ingress' error spans versus 17729.97 unset 'ingress' spans and 21.34 'router frontend egress' error spans versus 19057.38 unset egress spans (these are span counts, not request counts).

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 with duration ~15,000,000 us (e.g. spans 74de5b9996572945, 09efb3871d98224f, 83a6a06c508ba10b, http.status_code 504, otel.status_code ERROR), each paired with a 'router frontend egress' child span of 15,000,xxx us carrying error=true and http.status_code 0 - i.e. the proxy's 15s upstream response timeout fired; one 500 was also seen (span 79162c5b7c7f02c3, 8,549,452 us, http.status_code 500).

frontend-proxy's access log names the timing-out routes: '"GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 14999' and '"GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000', while in the same minutes '"GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 ... 26', '"POST /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 200 ... 5-180', '"GET /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 200 ... 3' and '"GET /api/data?... HTTP/1.1" 200 ... 3' all succeeded via_upstream.

frontend's own server spans hang for 15s while its inner route work never completes: p90 of frontend span 'GET' was 81-230ms before the onset and 15000ms in the 5-minute windows ending 07:01:08 and 07:06:08; 'POST' went 298-332ms -> 15000ms; 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' went ~460-554ms -> 15000ms; the client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' went 378-640ms -> 15000ms; and frontend 'tcp.connect' measured 15000ms in the window ending 07:01:08. 'GET /api/products/{productId}', 'GET /api/recommendations' and 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' produced no completions at all after ~07:01.

Sampled traces show the same shape from the client side: load-generator 'GET' spans of 15,001,860-15,002,511 us with http.status_code 504, frontend 'GET' spans of 15,000,255-15,014,207 us recorded as http.status_code 200, frontend-proxy ingress 504s and 'router frontend egress' 15,000,xxx us with http.status_code 0, while the same traces' POST /api/cart and grpc CartService calls complete in 1,227-382,347 us with grpc status 0.

checkout's own client span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' failed with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and otel.status_description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer' (durations 8,450,618 / 20,000,730 / 37,504,947 us), which surfaced as 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' rpc.grpc.status_code 13 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"0PUK6V6EV0"' and frontend 'POST /api/checkout' http.status_code 500.

The address being reset, 100.64.188.136:8080, is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP and port (service product-catalog, clusterIP 100.64.188.136, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog); the product-catalog pod itself is product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 with podIP 100.96.4.247.

product-catalog stopped working during the alert window: its container produced 9,443 log lines in the 06:40-07:11 range ('Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...', 'Loaded 10 products') and the newest of them is 2026-11-15T07:01:21.521305Z, i.e. no later line exists in the window although the ten-second reload lines had been continuous up to then; its span rate fell from 3.8/s (window ending 07:01:08) to 0/s (window ending 07:11:08).

Chaos Mesh PodNetworkChaos events name the product-catalog pod as their object: events of kind PodNetworkChaos with reason 'Updated' and message 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' whose involvedObject is pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 occur at 06:54:07, 06:55:02, 06:55:07, 06:56:02, 06:56:07, 06:57:02, 06:57:07, 06:58:02, 06:58:07, 06:59:02, 06:59:07, 07:00:02, 07:00:07, 07:01:02, 07:01:07, 07:02:02 and 07:02:07 UTC - starting about two minutes before the alert's 06:56:08 onset; the only other events in the otel-demo namespace in the window are the fraud-detection container's Pulled/Created/Started at 06:50:23.

The product-catalog pod shows no resource-exhaustion signature: container CPU usage fell from 0.0073 cores (5 min ending 06:46:08) to 0.0003 cores (ending 07:11:08), CFS throttled-period ratio fell from 0.1907 to 0.0293, working set stayed at 12.1-13.4 MiB against a 30Mi memory limit, and the pod is Running with all conditions True and restartCount 0 with no last termination state.

The collapse is broad in span volume but only a few operations show their own errors: in the 10 minutes ending 07:11:08 the per-service span rate fell to near zero for product-catalog (0/s), recommendation (0/s), checkout (0.21/s), accounting/currency/email/shipping/quote (0.004-0.008/s) and frontend (3.36/s), while positive error rates were recorded only for frontend-proxy 'ingress' (1.907/s), frontend 'GET'/'POST'/'POST /api/checkout'/'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' (0.018-0.174/s), frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (0.095/s), 'router frontend egress' (0.038/s), fraud-detection/ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (0.0018/s) and recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (0.0018/s).

checkout itself kept processing orders until the product-catalog failures became general: its log shows 'payment went through' / 'order placed' / 'order confirmation email sent' repeatedly through 2026-11-15T07:00:59Z, and thereafter only '[PlaceOrder]' entries up to 07:02:17 without succeeding orders in the newest 120 lines.

Most likely causal chain: product-catalog became unreachable around 06:54-06:56 and then stopped answering entirely after 07:01:21, so every caller that needs it hangs - frontend /api/products/{id} and /api/recommendations requests (which time out at frontend-proxy's 15s limit and become the 504 error spans driving the alert) and checkout's ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls (gRPC 14 connection reset -> PlaceOrder 13 -> frontend 500). Home page, cart and /api/data paths that do not need product-catalog stayed at 200, which is consistent with this being a dependency-specific fault rather than a frontend or proxy failure.

Best-supported deepest cause: a network fault injected on the product-catalog pod by Chaos Mesh (PodNetworkChaos) starting 2026-11-15T06:54:07Z is what made product-catalog unreachable - clients see connection resets to the product-catalog Service IP and product-catalog simultaneously stops logging and stops producing spans while its container stays alive, unscheduled-free and resource-idle. Because the PodNetworkChaos spec could not be read, the specific action (loss, delay, partition or reset) remains unverified.

A remaining alternative for the product-catalog silence is that the product-catalog process itself is blocked (all goroutines stalled, including its roughly ten-second catalog-reload logger) rather than merely network-isolated; the log gap 06:56:16-06:59:50 followed by a burst of eight 'Product Found' lines at 06:59:50, and the later permanent silence, fit both a partially lossy network fault and an internally blocked process, and the available evidence cannot distinguish them.

CPU throttling / CPU-limit starvation of product-catalog is not supported: its throttled-period ratio was at most 0.19 and its CPU usage ~7m of a 15m limit before the incident, and both fell (to ~0.03 and ~0.3m) while it was silent, so the container was idle, not saturated, when it stopped answering.

An OOMKill or crash-loop of product-catalog is not supported: the container's restartCount is 0, its lastState has no terminated entry, every pod condition including Ready is True, and its working set stayed at 12.1-13.4 MiB against a 30Mi limit.

The fraud-detection OOMKill during the window is a separate, recovered event, not the cause of these 504s: that container's last termination reason was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 finishedAt 06:50:22Z and it restarted at 06:50:23Z (restartCount 2, now Running and Ready), and checkout continued to log completed orders ('payment went through', 'order placed') at 06:58:55-07:00:59 after that restart, while the failing calls observed are ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, not payment or fraud-detection.

frontend and frontend-proxy pods themselves show no restart or crash evidence: frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, and the frontend's memory working set rose from ~126MiB (06:41) to ~173MiB (07:06) against a 200Mi limit, which is consistent with accumulated hung requests rather than a pod failure.

gaps: The PodNetworkChaos object itself could not be read: chaos-mesh custom resources are not among the kinds the Kubernetes tool exposes (the CRD listing attempt was refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE), so the fault's action/direction/target selector/duration and whether the experiment is still active are unknown; only controller 'Updated' events naming the product-catalog pod are visible.
The change-history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who applied the chaos experiment, when, and whether it was intended could not be checked.

Whether product-catalog recovered after the observed window is unknown: no product-catalog log line or span exists after 07:01:21Z within the window (through 07:11:45Z), while the last PodNetworkChaos event is 07:02:07Z, so fault end and recovery are unverified; a later fetch for 07:01:25-07:11:45Z logs returned no_data, which is not evidence of absence.

The frontend container wrote no readable stdout lines in 06:30-07:11:45Z (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data), so frontend-side application logging could not be checked; frontend evidence is limited to its spans.

gRPC-level metrics rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series in the window, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="otel-demo"} returned no series, so those corroborating views are unknown rather than zero.

recommendation's own health is not established: its logs in 06:50-07:11:45Z contained 226 lines, none matching error keywords, and its newest line is 06:54:57Z; its span rate fell to 0/s, but no recommendation-side error signal was observed, so it is neither confirmed affected nor cleared.

Trace evidence is a biased sample (spans_shown vs spans_omitted, sampled traces only), and span counts are not request counts; the alert's own 'current: 1.422' figure was not independently reproduced - the measured frontend-proxy 'ingress' error span rate peaked at 1.933/s and 1.632/s in 5-minute windows.

Root-cause detail below 'product-catalog unreachable' (exact packet-level fault, or whether the product-catalog process is internally blocked) cannot be determined from spans, logs or cAdvisor metrics available here.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos Mesh PodNetworkChaos/PodChaos resources in namespace otel-demo (spec.action, direction, selector, duration, status) to confirm the injected fault type and whether the experiment has ended.

Verify product-catalog reachability directly after the window (e.g. connect to product-catalog.otel-demo:8080 and issue a ListProducts/GetProduct call from another pod) and capture a goroutine/pprof dump if requests hang, to separate network isolation from an internally blocked process.

Correlate with the change/CI pipeline or chaos scheduler that created the product-catalog PodNetworkChaos around 2026-11-15T06:54Z, since the experiment - not the demo application code - appears to be the trigger.

If the experiment has ended and product-catalog is still silent, restart the product-catalog pod and confirm that /api/products/{id} and /api/recommendations latency and frontend-proxy 504s return to their pre-06:56 baseline.
